title: Postmortem: 2024-05-14 burst-traffic outage
author: Rohan Iyer
body:
## Summary
On 2024-05-14 14:22 UTC, Events service degraded for 47 minutes; full outage 14:38–14:50. Triggered by a 3x batch from Hooli combined with a race condition in rate limiter v1. Five customers tripped SLA (Hooli, Globex, Umbrella, Tyrell, three SMBs).

## Timeline (UTC)
- 14:20 — Hooli batch kicks off.
- 14:22 — Events latency p99 begins climbing.
- 14:25 — Mei pages, declares incident, Rohan takes IC.
- 14:33 — Root cause hypothesis: rate limiter pass-through.
- 14:38 — Full outage as connection pool exhausts.
- 14:42 — Mitigation deployed (hard-cap on Hooli key).
- 14:50 — Service recovering.
- 15:09 — Fully recovered.

## Root cause
Rate limiter v1 implements a token-bucket in Redis. Bucket refill uses GET → compute → SET, not atomic. Under concurrent burst from a single tenant, multiple workers see an old bucket state and each let a request through, even when budget is exhausted. Effective ceiling becomes ~Nx workers under burst, not the configured limit.

We knew this was theoretically possible (called out in code comments). Real-world incidence required a 3x burst against a tenant whose normal limit was already close to ceiling. Hooli is the only tenant that fits that profile today.

## Why didn't tests catch this?
Unit tests exercised the math, not the concurrency. Load tests use a single client which serializes the calls. Real burst behavior emerges only under multi-pod concurrency.

## Why did the impact spread beyond Hooli?
No per-tenant connection-pool isolation in Events service. Hooli exhausted shared pool, took everyone down.

## Action items
1. Open rate-limiter-v2 project. Move to leaky-bucket using Redis Lua scripts (atomic). **Owner: Ankur, review: Rohan. By 2024-08.**
2. Per-tenant connection-pool isolation in Events service. **Owner: Maya. By 2024-Q3.**
3. Add multi-client concurrent burst harness to load test suite. **Owner: Mei. By 2024-06-15.**
4. Customer SLA-credit memo. **Owner: Lena/Priya. By 2024-05-20.**

## What went well
- Time-to-detect (3 min) and time-to-mitigate (20 min) acceptable.
- Cross-team coordination (engineering + CSM) worked — Lena had customer comms ready before the incident channel even slowed down.

## What didn't
- The race condition was a known-known. We carried it. We shouldn't have.
- Connection-pool isolation has been on the backlog for 9 months.

## Followup commitment
This is not the kind of bug we should be writing postmortems on. Rate-limiter-v2 is the priority project for the platform team this quarter.

title: Rate limiter v2 — kickoff & scope
discussion:
Rohan opened with intent: smallest version of v2 that actually fixes the race. Not a redesign of every rate-limiting need we have ever had.

Ankur proposed leaky-bucket in Redis using Lua for atomicity. Rohan agreed but wanted to see one alternative before committing — token-bucket atomicized via Lua. Ankur to spike both for a week and report back.

Maya raised cross-region sync — current limits are per-region, multi-region usage of the same tenant gets multiplied silently. Rohan flagged as known issue, explicitly out of scope for v2: 'we don't fix two things at once. Cross-region is a v2.1 conversation. I'd rather ship v2 in 8 weeks than v2-with-everything in 16.'

Mei raised the load-test harness from the postmortem AI; she'll have it ready before v2 lands so we can prove the fix.

Devika asked about backwards compatibility. Rohan: 'config interface stays the same. Tenants don't see anything except correct enforcement.'
decisions: Spike: leaky-bucket Lua vs token-bucket Lua, 1 week, owner Ankur
OUT OF SCOPE for v2: cross-region limit sync (logged as v2.1 work)

title: RFC: ratelimit-v2
author: Ankur Bose
body:
## TL;DR
Replace v1 token-bucket (Redis GET/SET, not atomic) with leaky-bucket implemented as a single Lua script in Redis. Drop-in compatible config. Ship by end of Q3.

## Algorithm choice — leaky vs token (atomic)
Spiked both with Lua atomicity. Both correct under burst.

Leaky-bucket wins on:
- Smoother request shaping (no burst-at-T0 pattern that token-bucket allows).
- Simpler ops mental model — 'rate at which traffic drains' is a single number.
- Edge case: tenants who legitimately want bursts can configure a higher base rate. We lose the 'free burst budget' that token-bucket provided. None of our current customers depend on that explicitly.

Decision: leaky-bucket Lua.

## Implementation
- Single Lua script: takes (tenant_id, cost), returns (allowed: bool, retry_after_ms: int).
- Redis key: `ratelimit:{tenant_id}`. Hash with `level` and `last_drain_ts`.
- Drain rate = configured limit per second.
- Bucket capacity = drain rate * burst_seconds (configurable, default 10s).

## Migration
- v2 code path behind feature flag, per-tenant.
- Roll out 1% → 10% → 50% → 100% over 2 weeks.
- Both v1 and v2 emit the same metrics so dashboards stay valid.

## Out of scope
- Cross-region limit sync. Tracked as ratelimit-v2.1.

## Risks
- Lua script in Redis blocks other commands during execution. Script measured at 0.4ms p99, well under threshold.
- Time skew between Redis and app pods. Use Redis time only inside script.

subject: ratelimit-v2 rollout complete — 100%
body:
Rohan,

Finished the 100% cutover Friday. Two weeks at 100%, no incidents. Mei's burst harness now passes consistently — v1 used to fail it.

Closing the project. Cross-region sync issue is in the backlog as ratelimit-v2.1. Maya owns long-term.

Thanks for the reviews.

— Ankur

subject: Re: ratelimit-v2 rollout complete — 100%
body:
Nice work, Ankur. Closing out the postmortem AI as well.

For the record on the v2.1 cross-region sync: the trade is straightforward — multi-region usage by the same tenant currently gets effectively N x configured limit (one bucket per region). Acceptable today because (a) only 4 tenants spread across regions, and (b) we'd notice from billing-side anomalies before customer-side anomalies. Real fix requires Redis CRDT or a control plane that owns global token budget. Not this quarter.

Maya — when you take the v2.1 work, the cheapest version is probably 'global limit configurable separately from per-region', not full cross-region atomicity. Worth talking through before designing.

—r

title: Postmortem: 2025-05-22 Hooli rate-limit cascade
author: Rohan Iyer
body:
## Summary
On 2025-05-22 17:14 UTC, Hooli traffic began returning high rate of 429s. Limit had not been updated to reflect their Q1 expansion (2x seats, ~1.7x API usage). Misconfiguration tripped a global circuit breaker downstream that affected ~9% of API traffic for 38 minutes.

## Customer impact
- Hooli: primary, 38 min of mostly-blocked traffic.
- ~9% of other tenants: brief degradation (1–4 min) as global breaker tripped.
- Priya managed Hooli comms in parallel; Lena coordinated SLA credits.

## Root cause
1. **Misconfiguration**: Hooli's per-tenant limit was set during onboarding in 2023. Q1 2025 expansion didn't trigger a config review. No automation links seat-count to limit.
2. **Cascade via global breaker**: Gateway has a global circuit breaker that trips when any single tenant produces > 30% of total 429s. Designed for tenant-isolation but in this case the tenant was producing legitimate traffic, just over their limit.

## Action items
1. **Auto-adjust limits on contract change**. Owner: Ankur. By 2025-Q3.
2. **Alerting on tenant approaching configured limit (90%)**. Owner: Mei. By 2025-06-15.
3. **Reconsider global circuit breaker behavior under legit-traffic-over-limit**. Owner: Maya. Open RFC. By 2025-Q3.
4. **SLA credit to Hooli**. Owner: Priya/Lena.

## Reflection
rate-limiter-v2 fixed the race-condition class of bug. This is a different class — operational + design. v2.1 (cross-region) is still on the backlog; this incident isn't directly that, but it points at the same theme: we need the rate limiter to be more aware of who tenants are and what they bought, not just a number in a config.

title: Platform handoff — Rohan → Maya — rate limiter & events
discussion:
Rohan walked Maya through the rate limiter history: v1 race incident May 2024 → ratelimit-v2 leaky-bucket Lua, owned by Ankur, shipped Aug 2024. v2.1 cross-region sync still open — Rohan recommends 'global limit + per-region config' as the cheapest correct version, not full CRDT.

2025-05-22 incident is the more interesting recent context — exposed the 'limits aren't tied to contracts' design gap. Maya now owns Action Item 3 (circuit breaker behavior under legit overage) — Rohan strong opinion: don't rip out the global breaker, but exempt traffic that's legitimately over a contracted limit (vs malicious or buggy). Talk to Sasha for the security framing.

Events store: ADR-0017 still holds. Tarun's spike May 2025 confirmed Postgres still wins at current volume. Re-trigger is sustained 60M/day or replica p95 > 8s on aggregations. Maya should re-spike when triggered, not before.

Backlog priorities Maya inherits: (1) ratelimit-v2.1, (2) circuit breaker policy, (3) per-tenant pool isolation completion (still partial), (4) eventually ClickHouse.

Devika asked about juniors. Rohan: 'Ankur is excellent — give him the ratelimit-v2.1 design lead. Bryan needs a stretch project — SDK telemetry rewrite is sized right.'
decisions: Maya is platform tech lead effective 2025-12-15
Rohan available for async questions through 2025-12-31; emergencies after via Devika
